messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: High latency detected for Meridian Bank (vpc-prod-eu-central) — p99 spike > 3s across dedicated pool id dp-42. Auto-escalating to oncall.

maya: oncall here, seeing the alert. pulling up dashboards now.

daniel: i'm going to join — taking 2min. any customer impact noted?

maya: p95 at ~450ms but p99 just jumped to ~3.4s for last 5m. error rate is stable (0.2%), so this looks like pure latency, not errors.

li: logs show a lot of KV cache misses for Meridian tenant keys around the spike window. I'm attaching a sample tail:```
[2026-03-15T08:12:01Z] req_id=abb12 tenant=meridian db_get cache_miss
[2026-03-15T08:12:01Z] req_id=abb13 tenant=meridian model=redwood-large seq=1024 tokens=64
```

ash: Meridian is on a dedicated pool dp-42 in eu-central1 with pinned model redwood-large-8q. No recent deploys recorded in that pool in last 24h.

maya: sara_meridian — are you seeing customer-side retries or reports?

sara_meridian: We started getting user complaints ~08:10 UTC. Some pages say UI timeouts. We're throttling client retries but need an ETA.

daniel: assigning roles: i'll handle pool-level mitigation (scaling / routing), @li pls investigate cache miss root cause and KV latency. @maya pls coordinate customer comms and confirm isolation.

maya: on it. I'll DM Sara a short status update and ETA.

li: quick observation: KV store (managed by customer) shows increased 99th percentile of GET latency around the same range (2.5s). Our serving runtime falls back to model recompute when KV misses happen which amplifies token generation latency.

daniel: ok, that suggests external dependency issue. Immediate mitigations we can do from our side: 1) enable tenant-specific local caching (tx-cache) for Meridian on dp-42, 2) scale the dedicated pool by +2 replicas, 3) route a small fraction of traffic to the eu-west-1 warm fallback pool with identical model. Which do we want to run in parallel?

maya: recommend parallel: scale pool and enable tx-cache, and start warm-fallback routing at 10% as canary. we want to avoid full region failover unless needed.

ash: executing scale: hitting dedicated orchestration API now:```bash
rictl pools scale --pool dp-42 --replicas 4
```

incident-bot: deployment job started: scale-job-1882005432-1 (eta ~45s).

li: enabling tx-cache for Meridian on dp-42: applying config patch to runtime.```json
{"tenant":"meridian","tx_cache":true,"ttl_ms":600000}
```

daniel: starting gradual route to eu-west-1 fallback:```yaml
- match: tenant == "meridian"
  route: primary: dp-42
  fallback: dp-56-eu-west-1
  fallback_percent: 10
```

maya: I told Sara we'll have a mitigation in place in ~5-10min and we're monitoring. she asked for confirmation we won't do a full region failover without approval.

sara_meridian: confirmed — please do canary routing only. we can open to failover if things worsen.

ash: scale finished; new replicas `dp-42-replica-3` & `dp-42-replica-4` are up and warmed. health checks OK.

incident-bot: scale-job-1882005432-1: SUCCESS.

li: tx-cache enabled and warmed. initial cache hit rate for Meridian moved from 12% to 62% after priming.

daniel: routing to fallback put into place at 10%. starting to monitor metrics.

maya: early signs: p99 dropped from 3.4s -> 1.2s in last 2m. p95 steady ~420ms. Sara, did your UI error reports drop?

sara_meridian: yes — complaints dropping. some users still seeing timeouts but much better. thank you.

li: note in logs we're still seeing intermittent KV latency spikes from customer-side datastore. we've added a note to the incident ticket for postmortem and suggested KV autoscaling recommendations.

daniel: next steps: keep fallback at 10% for 15m, keep tx-cache enabled, keep pool at scaled size. if p99 holds <1.5s for 10m, we'll start ramping fallback down. also add a temporary per-tenant soft QPS limit to reduce thundering herd on KV:```bash
rictl tenants set-qps --tenant meridian --qps 2500
```

maya: applying qps limit now. informing Sara. also scheduling a brief handoff to the day oncall in 20m.

ash: qps limit applied. no immediate errors.

incident-bot: alert muted for Meridian p99 while mitigations active (alert-channel: incidents).

daniel: summary for post-incident notes: root cause likely external KV datastore p99 latency increase causing cache misses which cascaded into model recompute latency in dedicated pool. Mitigations: tx-cache, pool scale, 10% fallback routing, tenant QPS cap. Follow-ups: advise customer KV autoscaling + add cross-region KV fallback pattern, consider automatic tx-cache enablement when cache miss rate > X.

maya: will draft customer-facing timeline and postmortem. moving to monitoring-only channel in 30m if stable. thanks all for fast responses. :thumbsup:

sara_meridian: appreciate the rapid fix. will coordinate on our side for KV autoscaling.

incident-bot: thread closed to active paging at 1882005600.
